title: Typed absence and wire shape
summary: A domain-neutral TypeScript adapter preserves omission, explicit clear, an intentionally empty object, and meaningful falsy values as distinct JSON update instructions.

use.practicalQuestion: How can a JSON update boundary preserve the difference among an omitted field, an explicit clear, an intentionally empty collection, and meaningful falsy values?
use.changedAbility: A collaborator can inspect and run one strict object-to-JSON adapter that assigns field-level meaning before serialization, keeps every admitted presence state distinct, and returns structured error paths that name the responsible field.
readers: AI collaborators implementing or reviewing JSON update boundaries
Technical practitioners evaluating optional-field and serialization behavior

provenance.description: Recurring human practice with JSON integrations informs this independently authored, company-neutral exemplar. Its code, names, and route-configuration fixtures are realistic synthetic material; operational schemas, private locators, endpoints, credentials, production records, and employer code remain with their authorized owners.
provenance.temporalScope: This version is a portable Node.js 22 and TypeScript 5.9.3 example of one in-memory object-to-JSON boundary. Network transport, persistence, generated clients, schema evolution, and authorization remain receiving-system concerns.

technicalVeracity.basis: Strict compilation and focused Node.js tests establish admitted optional-property types, exact fixture and expected bytes, one enumerable descriptor snapshot, own-property presence, JSON round-trip behavior, negative-zero normalization, detached frozen null-prototype output, structured error paths, and explicit rejection of unknown, symbolic, accessor-backed, undefined, misplaced-null, and invalid field values in the resolved environment.

environmentNotes: The runtime adapter imports no third-party package; the artifact-local development lock supplies the exact TypeScript compiler.
The example covers passive same-realm plain records and enumerable own data properties under one JavaScript process; executable proxies and cross-realm objects remain receiving-boundary questions.

reviewQuestions: Which fields distinguish omission, explicit clear, and an intentionally empty value?
Does the receiving transport preserve every state admitted by the source type?
Can validation inspect object shape without invoking caller-supplied accessors?
Which meanings belong to the named presence case rather than JavaScript truthiness?
decisionRules: Assign presence meaning per field before projecting a wire object.
Use own-property inspection to distinguish omission from a present value.
Reject present undefined at a JSON boundary and preserve admitted falsy values exactly.
Detach admitted nested data before returning a stable wire snapshot.

semanticMarkers.meaning: One presence-meaning map and one explicit projector preserve every meaning-bearing presence state through the object-to-JSON boundary.
Truthiness checks and broad defaulting collapse zero, false, an empty string, omission, and explicit clear into fewer states than the receiving contract provides.

One enumerable descriptor snapshot, field-level parsers, strict optional-property types, structured error paths, detached null-prototype objects, and focused round-trip tests keep each instruction legible.

instructionYields.instruction: Name each field's presence policy, then project only admitted own data properties into a detached wire object.
Exercise omission, null, empty object, zero, false, empty string, present undefined, unknown keys, accessors, and invalid field types.
Carry the same meanings through the API schema, generated client, transport, persistence layer, and receiver before adapting this example.

practice.codeExemplarGranularity: One self-contained TypeScript object-to-JSON adapter with a composite realistic synthetic fixture, an exact expected result, runtime tests, and compile-time contract tests.
practice.complexityAndAllocation: The projector performs one bounded pass over top-level keys, field-specific validation, and one bounded pass over headers. It allocates a detached header object and output object so the accepted snapshot remains stable after caller mutation.

boundaries.evidence: The checks establish the declared optional-property and object-to-JSON behavior for passive same-realm plain records, enumerable own data properties, the listed presence meanings, JSON-stable negative zero, structured error paths, and null-prototype output in the resolved Node.js and TypeScript environment.
boundaries.trust: The route configuration and values are realistic synthetic material. The example establishes representation behavior; authenticated origin, caller authority, and business acceptance remain separate trust decisions.
boundaries.transfer: A receiving system selects its API schema, generated-client contract, validation messages, authorization, schema evolution, concurrency, transport, and persistence behavior, then verifies that every admitted presence state survives the complete route.

failureModes: A caller can supply a present value that JSON cannot represent.
Broad defaulting can replace meaningful zero, false, or empty-string instructions.
An accessor or caller-owned nested object can make projection depend on later or implicit behavior.
A receiving layer can collapse states that the source adapter keeps distinct.
recoveryMoves: Return the exact field owner and require an admitted JSON value.
Apply the named presence meaning and retain each admitted falsy value.
Read enumerable own data properties and detach nested data into the accepted snapshot.
Add an end-to-end conformance case at every transport or persistence boundary that transforms the patch.
